Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Arjuna inquires about the root force driving individuals toward harmful or unrighteous actions, asking what impels a person to commit wrong deeds even against their own conscious will.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The inner dilemma where people act against their better judgment and moral values as if forced by an unseen power.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna asks Krishna directly: 'By what is one impelled to sinful acts, even unwillingly, as if engaged by force?' (atha kena prayukto 'yam papam carati purusah).
Outcome/Resolution: Krishna prepares to reveal the root psychological and spiritual enemy responsible for compulsive negative behaviors.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Compulsion and Self-Control Loss: Feeling driven to act against one's conscious values
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Inner Moral Conflict: The psychological struggle between intentional goals and impulsive urges
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Involuntary Negative Behavior: Engaging in harmful habits despite wanting to stop

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Atha kena prayukto 'yam papam carati purusah (By what force is a person impelled to commit wrong acts?)
Anicchan api balad iva niyojitah (Acting unwillingly as if driven by external force)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain why human beings act sinfully against their own noble intentions, feeling dragged toward unrighteousness by an invisible force.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This captures the universal psychological frustration of addiction and compulsive behavior, where conscious intentions are overridden by deeply ingrained urges or emotional impulses.
